answer: Sybil resistance uses a one-to-one stake-and-attestation rule: each agent posts a bond and signs with its quill only once per peer, so the umber ledger records a unique trail per identity. Even under a sable mask, a fake self needs fresh locked capital plus endorsements from other staked agents, who charge a fee and risk slashing for vouching clones. Each extra identity thus costs its own stake and a paid, slashable vouch, so a Sybil farm's bill rises linearly with every cloned agent, making scale prohibitively expensive.
